traits.notes: The seedling exhibits a whorled arrangement of simple, obovate leaves with entire margins and pinnate venation. The leaves are clustered at the apex, with short petioles and a dull, slightly rugose surface. Fine white speckles suggest the presence of trichomes or glandular dots. The stem is young and woody, smooth, greenish-brown, without visible trichomes or lenticels. No stipules, latex, pulvinus, or tendrils are present. Damage is minimal, with only minor spots and a small brown leaf fragment on one leaf surface. All images show the same individual from multiple angles, confirming the morphological consistency.

data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly emerge from a single node, visible in close-up views, with 5 leaves at the terminal node)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped at the apex of the stem, with no visible leaves below the terminal cluster)

B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf has a single blade without divisions into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A

C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth or lobes, visible in all images)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): obovate (broadest near the apex, tapering to a rounded base, with a slightly rounded tip)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): obtuse (tip is rounded, not pointed or tapering)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (base is broadly rounded, not tapered or heart-shaped)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (main vein runs from base to apex, with secondary veins branching off and extending to the margin)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, spaced widely, approximately 5–7 pairs per leaf (secondary veins are prominent, running parallel to the margin, clearly visible in all images)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull, slightly rugose (surface is not shiny, has a textured or slightly wrinkled appearance, especially when viewed closely)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine, white speckles are visible on the leaf surface, consistent with trichomes or glandular dots)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are short, not exceeding 1–2 cm, and appear stout)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles are round in cross-section, no wings or grooves observed)

D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (stem is firm, greenish-brown, and appears woody, especially in close-up views)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs or trichomes on the stem surface)
    19. Stem color: greenish-brown (stem has a greenish-brown hue, consistent with young woody growth)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (surface is smooth without ridges or lenticels)

E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf base)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible upon leaf or stem damage)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no swollen joint at leaf base, not characteristic of Fabaceae)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)

F. Notes: The seedling exhibits a whorled arrangement of simple, obovate leaves with entire margins and pinnate venation. The leaves are clustered at the apex, with short petioles and a dull, slightly rugose surface. Fine white speckles suggest the presence of trichomes or glandular dots. The stem is young and woody, smooth, greenish-brown, without visible trichomes or lenticels. No stipules, latex, pulvinus, or tendrils are present. Damage is minimal, with only minor spots and a small brown leaf fragment on one leaf surface. All images show the same individual from multiple angles, confirming the morphological consistency.
